- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase forecast to align with recent downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from midpoint of sentiment transition.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with that average unless sentiment strongly contradicts.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for low sentiment bias.
